requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1
requirements.summary: ufw was activated with 'ufw --force enable', confirmed active and 'enabled on system startup' (cmd-20acbe8ee7974a92), and systemctl is-enabled ufw returned 'enabled' (cmd-7ab9602e9bd54bc1). Persistence was directly demonstrated: node1 was rebooted via shutdown -r now, boot_id changed from d08fb446... to 3e0c0a29... (cmd-e7643ab148044b88, cmd-c31164c10af04c8e, cmd-f37c62b8bb5948a8), and post-reboot ufw status showed all three rules intact and active (cmd-eea0ad223ec24c17), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check.

Rule '22 ALLOW IN Anywhere' (and v6 equivalent) is present (cmd-20acbe8ee7974a92). Functionally verified reachable from node3 (an external host) both pre-reboot (cmd-178b7face1654f8d) and post-reboot via node2's connectivity check (cmd-3ae325a997db4209) and node3's final check (cmd-bb0e14a7341c44b3).

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2
requirements.summary: Rule '9000/tcp ALLOW IN 10.100.193.11' (node2's IP) is present and ordered before the reject rule (cmd-20acbe8ee7974a92). Functionally verified: node2 successfully delivered a payload to node1:9000 both pre-reboot (cmd-139c9b23f7634b56, payload confirmed via cmd-399431cd25364926) and post-reboot (cmd-407906ddf45047ef, exit:0).

requirements.requirement: Reject TCP port 9000 from node3 and everywhere else
requirements.summary: Rule '9000/tcp REJECT IN Anywhere' (and v6) is present after the node2-allow rule, so it catches all other sources (cmd-20acbe8ee7974a92). Functionally verified node3 was rejected pre-reboot (cmd-88d1278673a24415, exit:1) and post-reboot, including a final cluster-wide check after all three nodes were restarted (cmd-a1af0aced7f049ed, cmd-bb0e14a7341c44b3).

overall_summary: All material outcomes for the node1 firewall task are satisfied with strong, directly observed evidence: correct ufw rules (SSH anywhere, 9000 only from node2, reject 9000 elsewhere), persistent enablement, and functional traffic tests both before and after an actual node1 reboot (with boot-identity change confirmed against the fixed lifecycle snapshot). The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on all three nodes with matching pre/post boot identities and recovered service state. Hygiene is very good aside from one leftover temp log file on node1.
limitations: The SSH-from-anywhere check relied on only one external source (node3) plus a self-check from node1; no additional external hosts were tested, though this is a reasonable proxy for 'any address' in this bounded topology.
The single leftover /tmp/nc9000b.log file on node1 was not independently confirmed to be harmless beyond visual inspection of the temp-file diff.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: default policy changes (deny incoming/allow outgoing) and three firewall rules were necessary prerequisites, and the ufw enable was required. Temporary nc listeners (cmd-7ab9602e9bd54bc1, cmd-6e5d8afd7adb4a64) used for functional verification were killed after use (cmd-399431cd25364926, cmd-acbd96347c2240a3), a legitimate bounded evidence-collection action. However, one artifact was left behind: /tmp/nc9000b.log from the second listener remained on node1 in the after-executor snapshot (only the process was killed, not the log file) - a minor, low-risk, unremoved residue. Provider-wide restart evidence was collected for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity and service-health checks, consistent with the fixed lifecycle cross-check data.
